easy.def: All the words that you know.
examples: I learn new vocabulary.
She has a big vocabulary.
We have a vocabulary test.

more.def: All the words that a person knows and uses, or a list of words with their meanings.
examples: Reading lots of books helps to build a big vocabulary.
We have a vocabulary test on Friday.
The baby's vocabulary grew to about fifty words.

easy.def: Of the voice or using the voice.
examples: The singer has a great vocal range.
He gave a vocal answer.
The vocal music was lovely.

more.def: Having to do with the voice, or speaking out loudly about something.
examples: The singer has a strong vocal talent.
She is very vocal about helping animals.
The choir sang a vocal piece without any instruments.

easy.def: What is popular at a time.
examples: Hats were in vogue.
That style is in vogue.
Short hair is in vogue.

more.def: The popular fashion at a certain time.
examples: Long scarves are in vogue this winter.
Hats were once in vogue.
That style was in vogue last year.

easy.def: The sound you make when you talk or sing.
examples: I have a loud voice.
Use your inside voice.
Her voice is sweet.

more.def: The sound that comes from a person's mouth when they speak or sing.
examples: The teacher has a calm, friendly voice.
I heard a voice calling from the garden.
Her singing voice is clear and high.

easy.def: A big empty space.
examples: Space is a void.
We looked into the void.
The cave was a dark void.

more.def: A large empty space with nothing in it.
examples: The astronaut gazed into the dark void of space.
A cold void opened up beneath the bridge.
The cave was a black void that seemed to go on forever.

easy.def: Of no use or force under a rule.
examples: The old ticket is void.
The contract is void.
The coupon is void.

more.def: Having no force or use under a rule or a contract.
examples: The coupon is void after the end of the month.
The contract was void because no one had signed it.
A ticket that is torn in half is void.

easy.def: Having to do with volcanoes.
examples: The island is volcanic.
We saw volcanic rock.
Volcanic ash fell.

more.def: Made by or having to do with volcanoes.
examples: The island was formed by volcanic action.
We found black volcanic rock on the beach.
Volcanic ash covered the town after the eruption.

easy.def: A mountain that can shoot out hot melted rock.
examples: The volcano had smoke on top.
Hot lava came out of the volcano.
The island has a volcano.

more.def: A mountain with an opening where melted rock, ash, and gas can burst out.
examples: When the volcano erupted, lava flowed down its sides.
The island was formed by a volcano long ago.
Ash from the volcano covered the nearby town.

easy.def: A small animal like a mouse with a short tail.
examples: A vole dug a hole.
The vole is small.
Voles eat seeds.

more.def: A small furry animal like a mouse, with a short tail, that lives in fields and eats plants.
examples: A vole scurried through the tall grass.
Owls hunt voles at night.
Voles dig little tunnels in the meadow.

easy.def: A hit of a ball before it touches the ground.
examples: She hit a volley.
The volley was long.
The tennis volley was great.

more.def: A hit of a ball before it bounces, or a rapid burst of many things at once.
examples: She hit a volley across the net.
A volley of questions came at the speaker.
The players hit a long volley over the net.

easy.def: A game where teams hit a ball over a net.
examples: We play volleyball.
The volleyball went over the net.
I like volleyball.

more.def: A game in which two teams hit a ball back and forth over a high net with their hands.
examples: We played volleyball on the beach.
In volleyball, a team gets three hits before the ball goes over.
She spiked the volleyball over the net.

easy.def: How loud a sound is.
examples: Turn down the volume.
The volume is loud.
The radio's volume is low.

more.def: How loud or quiet a sound is.
examples: Turn down the volume of the TV.
The volume on the radio was too high.
The teacher asked us to lower our volume.

easy.def: How much space something fills.
examples: The volume of the tank is large.
The cup's volume is one cup.
Find the volume.

more.def: The amount of space that something takes up or holds.
examples: The volume of the tank is fifty gallons.
We measured the volume of water in the cup.
The box has a large volume.

easy.def: A book.
examples: I read the first volume.
The set has ten volumes.
The library has old volumes.

more.def: One book in a set, or a book.
examples: I read the first volume of the series.
The scientist kept a volume of notes.
The library has old volumes of the news.

easy.def: Done because you want to, not because you have to.
examples: The club is voluntary.
A voluntary job.
It is voluntary.

more.def: Done by choice, not because someone makes you do it.
examples: Joining the chess club is voluntary, so you can choose to come.
She did voluntary work at the animal shelter on weekends.
Wearing a costume to school on Friday is voluntary.

easy.def: A person who does a job for free because they want to.
examples: A volunteer read to us.
She is a volunteer at the library.
Volunteers cleaned the park.

more.def: A person who chooses to do a job without pay to help others.
examples: A volunteer read stories to the kids at the library.
Volunteers helped clean up the beach.
The hospital has many volunteers.

easy.def: To offer to do something.
examples: I volunteered to help.
She volunteers at the shelter.
He volunteered to carry the bags.

more.def: To offer to do something without being asked or paid.
examples: He volunteered to carry the heavy bags.
She volunteers at the animal shelter on Saturdays.
I volunteered to clean the board.

easy.def: To throw up food from your stomach.
examples: I felt sick and vomited.
The dog vomited.
He vomited.

more.def: To bring up food from your stomach through your mouth.
examples: The baby vomited after drinking too fast.
I felt sick and almost vomited.
The dog vomited on the rug.

easy.def: To choose by raising a hand or marking a paper.
examples: We vote for class pet.
She voted for the red team.
Raise your hand to vote.

more.def: To show your choice by raising a hand or marking a ballot.
examples: Our class voted for a new pet.
Adults vote to choose a mayor.
Everyone voted to go to the park.

easy.def: A choice you make in a group.
examples: My vote is for pizza.
Each person gets a vote.
The vote was close.

more.def: A choice that you show in a group decision.
examples: My vote is for the pizza party.
Each student gets one vote.
The vote was close, but the red team won.

easy.def: A person who votes.
examples: The voter chose a name.
Every voter gets one vote.
The voters lined up.

more.def: A person who votes, or is allowed to vote, in an election.
examples: Each voter in the town marked a choice on the ballot.
Voters lined up outside the school to cast their votes.
My mom became a voter when she turned eighteen.

easy.def: To say that something is true or good.
examples: I vouch for him.
She vouched for her friend.
He vouches for the story.

more.def: To say that you believe someone or something is true or good.
examples: I can vouch for my friend; he is honest.
She vouched for the quality of the cake.
The teacher vouched for his good work.

easy.def: A paper that you can use instead of money.
examples: I got a voucher for free pizza.
Use this voucher at the shop.
The voucher is for one ice cream.

more.def: A printed paper that can be used in place of money to pay for something.
examples: Our class got a voucher for a free book at the fair.
The restaurant gave us a voucher for a free dessert.
She traded her voucher for a ticket to the show.

easy.def: A serious promise.
examples: He made a vow.
The vow was kept.
She made a vow to help.

more.def: A very serious promise that you make.
examples: He made a vow to keep the secret.
The knights made a vow to protect the king.
She kept her vow to visit her grandmother each week.

easy.def: To make a serious promise.
examples: I vow to help.
She vowed to be kind.
He vowed to try again.

more.def: To promise something very seriously.
examples: She vowed to keep the secret.
He vowed to try harder next time.
The knight vowed to protect the village.

easy.def: The letters a, e, i, o and u.
examples: "A" is a vowel.
Every word has a vowel.
The vowel is the letter "e."

more.def: A letter such as a, e, i, o or u that stands for an open speech sound.
examples: The letters a, e, i, o and u are vowels.
The word "cat" has the vowel "a."
We circled every vowel in the sentence.

easy.def: A long trip on a ship or in space.
examples: The ship went on a long voyage.
We read about a voyage to the moon.
The voyage took many days.

more.def: A long journey, especially by sea or through space.
examples: The voyage across the ocean took three weeks.
The explorers set off on a voyage around the world.
The spacecraft began its long voyage to Mars.
